insight.title: Why Removing Steps Makes You More Creative
insight.subtitle: How deleting a step solves problems faster than adding one

sections.text: Look at the most iconic products you own. Their biggest breakthroughs often didn't come from adding new features, but from removing them. We naturally favor addition, yet the most elegant innovation is usually subtraction.
Our brains are biologically biased to suggest more of something to fix a problem. We buy organizers for clutter or create rules for efficiency. Real creativity begins when you resist the urge to add.

Great decisions aren't made by considering every possible option, but by stripping away the noise. When you remove the non-essential, the best path forward finally becomes visible, allowing you to move much faster.
Try this today: When you face a complex task today, identify one step you can skip to reach the goal.
Innovation isn't what you build; it's what you have the courage to remove.

news.title: Meta, Microsoft plan cuts, buyouts that may affect 23,000 jobs amid AI push
news.description: Big tech companies are looking for ways to slash costs as they pour billions into data centres and other AI infrastructure.
news.why: Finding a job in the tech sector may become more difficult.

news.title: Oil rises above $106 per barrel as US, Iran deadlocked in Strait of Hormuz
news.description: Jump in prices comes as Donald Trump says vessels will need permission of US Navy to transit key waterway.
news.why: Your fuel and daily commuting costs may rise soon.

news.title: Israel defense minister says awaiting US green light to 'return Iran to Stone Age'
news.description: Defence minister Israel Katz said on Thursday that Israel was "prepared to resume the war against Iran", adding that his country was awaiting a green light from the United States to return Iran to "the Stone Age". FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.
news.why: Escalating conflict may drive up your energy and heating bills.

news.title: How the Iran war has stoked competition between India and China for Russian oil
news.description: As the Iran war drags on and the Strait of Hormuz stays shut, India and China are increasingly competing against each other for shrinking crude oil supplies.
news.why: Intense competition for fuel may keep your energy prices high.

news.title: UK: Health data volunteered by 500,000 people to Biobank charity listed for sale on Alibaba in China
news.description: The British government is investigating how health data volunteered to a charity for research purposes wound up for sale via three vendors on the Alibaba e-commerce site in China. One listing had 500,000 people's data.
news.why: Your private health information may be sold or misused by hackers.

news.title: G7 omits climate change from Paris talks to appease US, host France says
news.description: France is hosting a G7 meeting on the environment in Paris, omitting climate change from the agenda to avoid disputes with the US and preserve unity.
news.why: Delayed climate action may lead to more frequent and costly disasters.

news.title: John Ternus is officially Apple’s next CEO, iPhone 18 colors, iOS 27 rumors
news.description: Benjamin and Chance react to the biggest news of the week, and probably this year, with Tim Cook officially announcing his plans to hand over the CEO job to John Ternus. The calm and orchestrated transition falls directly into Cook’s playbook. Also, we have new leaks about iOS 27 and iPhone 18 Pro c
news.why: Your future Apple devices and software may change under new leadership.

news.title: TSMC hits fresh record high on new chip tech, Arizona expansion plan
news.why: Your next computer or smartphone may become easier to buy.

news.title: 'This is my home,' says DACA recipient deported then returned to U.S.
news.description: The Department of Homeland Security says it has deported more than 675,000 immigrants in the first year of Trump's second term. Although the administration claims to be targeting violent criminals, others continue to be caught in the crackdown, including some who are protected from deportation. Liz
news.why: Stricter immigration enforcement may reduce the workers providing your local services.

news.title: Supreme Court rules for Michigan in fight to shut down aging energy pipeline
news.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that Michigan's lawsuit to shut down an aging Enbridge pipeline beneath a Great Lakes channel will remain in state court.
news.why: Closing the pipeline may raise heating and fuel costs in Michigan.

news.title: Greenhouse gases from data center boom could outpace entire nations
news.description: Plants from OpenAI, Meta, xAI, and Microsoft could emit more than 129M tons annually.
news.why: Massive data center emissions may lead to higher electricity bills.

news.title: US Space Command: Russia is now operationalizing co-orbital ASAT weapons
news.description: "They’re putting operational systems up within orbit reach of our high-value satellites."
news.why: Attacks on satellites may disrupt your GPS and internet services.
